failedGraders: judge:A code REVIEW was just produced for a seeded /refunds PR in the React app. The diff under review is three files: packages/app/react/src/routes/(app)/refunds/index.tsx, packages/app/react/src/routes/(app)/refunds/-components/RefundTableSection/index.tsx, and packages/app/react/src/routes/(app)/refunds/refunds.pt.json. The reviewer's output is REVIEW.md at the repo root (read it AND the three seeded files AND, if helpful, the builder's final message). Judge the review for BOTH precision and recall against the route/react + component/react registries. The diff contains EXACTLY SIX genuine canon violations. The review PASSES recall only if it names ALL SIX (by the bp id OR by an unambiguous description of the same defect at the right location): (V1) the search schema in index.tsx composes the SDK params schema with .extend() instead of .and() (route bp-04 — .extend overwrites SDK field constraints). (V2) the route shell (RouteComponent) fetches the list via useListOrders and prop-drills data + search + onSearchParamsChange into RefundTableSection, instead of the section owning its own query and reading routeApi.useSearch()/navigate (route bp-02 / component bp-01 / CMP-P01 data ownership — the route must be a thin shell). (V3) RefundTableSection imports Trash from 'lucide-react' — mixed icon libraries; only @tabler/icons-react is sanctioned (component bp-03). (V4) StatusCell compares order.status === 'REFUNDED' with a literal string instead of PaymentStatusEnum.REFUNDED (component bp-14 — literal vs enum constant). (V5) StatusCell renders a hardcoded color-scale class (bg-blue-500 / text-white) instead of a design token or Badge variant (component bp-06). (V6) the first icon-only Button (the IconSend toggle) has no aria-label (component bp-17). The review PASSES precision only if it does NOT assert that any of these FOUR sanctioned shapes is a violation (each is a deliberate reverse-trap): (L1) const [menuOpen, setMenuOpen] = useState(false) is the ONE sanctioned useState — truly-local transient disclosure (state-placement case 5); it is NOT server data, NOT bookmarkable, NOT cross-component. Flagging it (e.g. "move to URL/store") is a false positive. (L2) the accented Portuguese copy lives in refunds.pt.json, the typed i18n catalog — the sanctioned home for copy. Only inline copy strings in .tsx code are violations. Flagging the JSON's accents/copy as hardcoded-string debt is a false positive. (L3) REFUND_STATUS_BADGE: Record<PaymentStatus, BadgeSpec> is an enum-keyed COLOR/VARIANT map colocated with the component — explicitly canon (icon/color/variant maps resolve to styles, not labels); its label values are i18n KEYS (enums.PaymentStatus.*), not inline copy. Flagging it as the banned Record<Enum,string> LABEL map (bp-23) is a false positive. (L4) StatusCell({ order }) receives its single item via prop because it is a leaf rendered N times inside the columns .map() (CMP-P05 — leaves take the item by prop). This is distinct from V2, which prop-drills the whole query response + search + callback into a Section. Flagging this leaf prop as prop-drilling is a false positive. VERDICT: PASS only if (recall) all six V1–V6 are named AND (precision) none of L1–L4 is asserted to be a violation AND the review's status is CHANGES_REQUESTED (a diff with six real defects cannot be APPROVED). Otherwise FAIL — name which Vs were missed and/or which Ls were wrongly flagged. Scope notes — judge the idiom, not the spelling: accept the violation named by bp id OR by a clear description at the right location (the reviewer need not quote the exact code); severity labels are the reviewer's call — do not fail on Major-vs-Blocker disagreement; a reviewer who NAMES a trap explicitly to CLEAR it ("useState here is fine because it's local disclosure", "this Record is a variant map, not a label map — fine") is doing the RIGHT thing — that is not a false positive, it is the calibrated behaviour, count it as correct precision; extra TRUE findings beyond the six (e.g. the section also lacks its own loading/skeleton, the route lacks errorComponent, the leaf badge text isn't from i18n) are NOT penalized as long as they are real and not one of the four traps; if the reviewer flags a real-but-minor nit that is genuinely a deviation (missing errorComponent is real route bp-05) that is fine; only the FOUR enumerated traps L1–L4 are false-positive bait. Do not invent NEW violations the registries don't list and hold the review to them.
